+# Incident Postmortem: Edge Client Request Jitter & High API Latency
+
+## Root Cause
+Commit `f1276612dfa530d4f49189c352014d3706ce7e24` ("Disable response caching") changed `CACHE_TYPE` in `api/config.py` from `"SimpleCache"` to `"NullCache"`. 
+Disabling response caching caused every request to `/v1/books/search` (which relies on `@cache.cached`) to perform a live, synchronous external metadata query via `BookProvider`. Under traffic generator load, the uncached requests overloaded the upstream metadata service (causing 503 errors) and exhausted Gunicorn worker processes. This caused P99 request latency on `booklogr-api` to spike to ~2.5s (threshold 300ms) and resulted in flapping request jitter on the edge client.
+
+## Evidence Used
+- **Alertmanager & Prometheus Signals**:
+  - `EdgeClientRequestJitter`: Flapping request jitter on edge client traffic.
+  - `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High`: P99 latency on `booklogr-api` reached 2.484s.
+  - `BookMetadataProviderErrorsElevated`: `book-metadata` provider returned elevated 5xx responses due to uncached query spikes.
+- **Prometheus Metric Inspection**:
+  - `flask_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{path="/v1/books/search"}` showed the vast majority of search requests taking between 0.25s and 2.5s.
+- **Git History**:
+  - `git log -p -n 10` revealed commit `f127661` which changed `CACHE_TYPE = "NullCache"`.
+
+## Changes Made
+- Modified `api/config.py` to restore response caching using `CACHE_TYPE = os.environ.get("CACHE_TYPE", "SimpleCache")`.
